guides.wedding-photo-collage.title: Wedding Photo Collage: Layouts That Print Well
guides.wedding-photo-collage.desc: Choose a wedding collage layout by aspect ratio and print size, keep consistent spacing, and avoid the mistakes that make a grid look crowded.
guides.wedding-photo-collage.lead: A collage reads as one image. Consistent gaps, a limited number of frames and a shared crop style matter more than the arrangement itself.
guides.wedding-photo-collage.f1v: 4:3, 3:2 and square are the safest print shapes
guides.wedding-photo-collage.f2v: Three to seven images reads better than twenty
guides.wedding-photo-collage.f3v: Use one gap value everywhere, scaled to the canvas
guides.wedding-photo-collage.f4v: Keep the same aspect ratio for every cell
guides.wedding-photo-collage.s1: Decide the final output size before placing photos. For a framed print, match a standard frame ratio and leave a small outer margin. Then crop every source image to the same cell shape so faces are treated consistently, and let one image be the anchor — usually a portrait at roughly twice the area of the others.
guides.wedding-photo-collage.s2: Common print sizes differ by region: the US uses inch sizes such as 8 × 10 and 11 × 14, while Europe uses A4, A3 and 20 × 30 cm. If you are ordering a canvas or a photo book spread, use the lab's exact pixel template rather than a generic ratio. For social sharing, a 4:5 portrait or 9:16 vertical fills more screen space than a square.
guides.wedding-photo-collage.s3: Avoid mixing landscape and portrait crops inside an unadjusted grid, which produces awkward empty strips. Keep the collage out of the bleed area, and do not place a face exactly on a seam. If the collage will be printed, export at 300 dpi and check it at actual size on paper — small faces that look fine on a phone disappear in print.
guides.wedding-photo-collage.q1: How many photos should a collage have?
guides.wedding-photo-collage.a1: Three to seven is a reliable range. Beyond that, each frame becomes too small to read, especially in print.
guides.wedding-photo-collage.q2: What size should I export for print?
guides.wedding-photo-collage.a2: 300 dpi at the final dimensions, for example about 2400 × 3000 pixels for an 8 × 10 inch print.
guides.wedding-photo-collage.q3: Should all photos have the same crop?
guides.wedding-photo-collage.a3: Yes. Consistent cell shape and spacing are what make a collage look designed rather than assembled.
